Apple filed a bombshell lawsuit against OpenAI on Friday, accusing the company of trade secret theft. There's plenty of juicy details in the initial draft of the complaint, but one figure jumped out at me: the number of former Apple employees now working at OpenAI.

400+ Apple employees now work at OpenAI

According to Apple's complaint, more than 400 former Apple employees now work at OpenAI. So Apple says it's "not surprising" that OpenAI employees have knowledge of Apple confidential information:

Given that more than 400 former Apple employees now work at OpenAI, it is not surprising that certain OpenAI personnel are familiar with Apple's confidential and proprietary information, information they were obligated to keep confidential. Yet rather than honor those obligations, OpenAI has instead leveraged that confidential information to extract even more from Apple's current employees and trusted partners—and designed its interview process to try to obtain additional Apple confidential information—all while attempting to conceal its actions. OpenAI currently employs former

While Apple didn't disclose specifics, we learned from a Bloomberg report that workers from "countless" teams inside Apple have jumped ship to OpenAI. Most recently, OpenAI poached Paul Meade, who worked on Apple Vision Pro and Apple's smart glasses project.

In fact, a Bloomberg report on Saturday said that "most" of OpenAI's hires from Apple came from the engineering organization led by Apple's incoming CEO, John Ternus. The report also noted that OpenAI's hardware chief, former Apple design lead Tang Tan, had a "tense" relationship with Ternus during his time at Apple.

It remains to be seen how Apple's lawsuit against OpenAI will shake out. Either way, it's sure to be a fascinating saga—especially if the case reaches the discovery stage. What are your thoughts on the suit? Let us know in the comments.
